title: Moonstone monster kit, format 1 (docs/MONSTER_KIT.md section 2.2)
description: One kit = a folder with kit.json (this schema) + PNG sheets.  Checked by tools/monsterkit/jsonschema_lite.py (a subset validator: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, min/max, pattern, oneOf, anyOf, $ref).  Cross-field rules (checklist per AI, palette classes, memory budgets) are monsterkit.py check, not JSON Schema.

name.description: identifier: lower case, digits, underscore; the base of the cel file names (<name>N.cel) and of the [creature <name>] row

ai.description: AI by name (ai_catalog.json ais); the checklist, tunables and the type byte follow it

scene.description: the original creature whose fight palette scene (indices 9..15) the kit uses, or a new scene row (9.5e2)

colors.description: the kit's palette as 12-bit RGB (editor working palette)

own.description: creature-owned colours: index (9..14 editable, 15 blood red) -> colour

celsets.description: up to 5 cel files = the 5 frame-set slots (LAB_05E0); draw opcodes $00..$10 are slot * 4

file.description: "auto" (<name>N.cel) or the original file name a T0 reskin replaces

hits.description: the set has a collide.hit set (attack points)

hit_name.description: the set's name line in collide.hit (matched case-insensitively), e.g. Troll1.cel

hit_frames.description: number of frames the original hit set lists (it can be shorter than the cel); the converter writes at least this many

roles.description: role name -> animation name (or, for walk.* tables, an array of animation names / null)

damage.description: damage by own action / 4 (only the entries the AI reads count: ai_catalog.json damage)

bank.description: an existing creature sound bank (ai_catalog.json sound_banks); new samples are out of scope for v1

origin.description: provenance of a game clone (written by monsterkit.py clone, read by check/build T0): the source creature, per cel file the sha1 of the file and of its decoded planes, the original frame sizes / plane bits / anchors, the colours the source art used (those stay legal even when they are forbidden classes), a hash of the source scripts, the source's stats and its largest per-tick draw area

rect.description: x, y, w, h in the sheet

png.description: alternative to src: a per-frame PNG (frames/NNN.png)

anchor.description: the frame's ground point; the converter emits dx = -anchorX, dy = -anchorY (dy fits s8)

type.description: the TT line of collide.hit (never read by the engine)

points.description: attack points x, y in 0..255 from the frame's top-left (bytes in the hit record)

nogore.description: flag $80: skipped when Gore is off

flags.description: raw flags byte (bits 2 / 3 have no name)

op.description: $A8 STORES (the low byte of) the value: it never ORs a bit

oneOf.description: an animation name: a script pointer (the original pokes +22 with script addresses)

ticks.description: fight frames ($FF markers) this step lasts

on_dead.description: animation to jump to (ifdead, $B4) when the owner's HP is <= 0: the die sequence

asm.description: opcodes the steps cannot express, in the tools/fightscript.py text syntax, kept verbatim so a clone converts back byte-identical
